es: Parafrasear y resumir lo que dice otra persona con verbos de habla (claim, point out, admit, suggest, deny, refuse, promise, warn) y su patrón.

teaching.en: Some experts claim that eight hours of sleep is excessive, yet the authors of the study maintain that most adults need it.
teaching.es: Algunos expertos afirman que ocho horas de sueño son excesivas, pero los autores del estudio sostienen que la mayoría de los adultos las necesita.
teaching.explanationEs: Claim that deja la duda sobre lo dicho; maintain that sostiene una postura pese a la oposición.
segments: Some experts claim that eight hours of sleep is excessive, yet
the authors of the study maintain that most adults need it.
teaching.audioText: Some experts claim that eight hours of sleep is excessive, yet the authors of the study maintain that most adults need it.

teaching.en: In the summary, critics point out that the sample was small, so the authors refuse to draw firm conclusions from it.
teaching.es: En el resumen, los críticos señalan que la muestra era pequeña, por lo que los autores se niegan a sacar conclusiones firmes.
teaching.explanationEs: Point out that + oración introduce un dato; refuse va seguido de to + verbo.
segments: In the summary, critics point out that the sample was small,
so the authors refuse to draw firm conclusions from it.
teaching.audioText: In the summary, critics point out that the sample was small, so the authors refuse to draw firm conclusions from it.

teaching.en: The minister was forced to acknowledge that the plan had failed, although she tried to downplay the scale of the losses.
teaching.es: La ministra se vio obligada a reconocer que el plan había fracasado, aunque intentó quitar importancia a la magnitud de las pérdidas.
teaching.explanationEs: Acknowledge that reconoce un hecho incómodo; downplay + nombre resta importancia.
segments: The minister was forced to acknowledge that the plan had failed,
although she tried to downplay the scale of the losses.
teaching.audioText: The minister was forced to acknowledge that the plan had failed, although she tried to downplay the scale of the losses.

teaching.en: Many users admit checking their phones at night, but some flatly deny doing it, even when the screen-time data says otherwise.
teaching.es: Muchos usuarios admiten mirar el móvil por la noche, pero algunos lo niegan rotundamente, incluso cuando los datos de uso dicen lo contrario.
teaching.explanationEs: Admit y deny se construyen con -ing cuando hablan de la propia acción del sujeto; flatly refuerza la negación.
segments: Many users admit checking their phones at night, but some flatly
deny doing it, even when the screen-time data says otherwise.
teaching.audioText: Many users admit checking their phones at night, but some flatly deny doing it, even when the screen-time data says otherwise.

teaching.en: Doctors suggest going to bed earlier, and they warn people against drinking coffee late in the evening.
teaching.es: Los médicos sugieren acostarse más temprano y advierten a la gente contra el café por la noche.
teaching.explanationEs: Suggest + -ing (nunca to + verbo); warn against + -ing advierte de un riesgo.
segments: Doctors suggest going to bed earlier, and they warn
people against drinking coffee late in the evening.
teaching.audioText: Doctors suggest going to bed earlier, and they warn people against drinking coffee late in the evening.

teaching.en: Some guests promise to reply later, but the host will not summarise the debate until every claim has been checked.
teaching.es: Algunos invitados prometen responder más tarde, pero la presentadora no resumirá el debate hasta que se compruebe cada afirmación.
teaching.explanationEs: Promise va seguido de to + verbo; en un resumen cada verbo de habla debe respetar lo que se dijo.
segments: Some guests promise to reply later, but the host will
not summarise the debate until every claim has been checked.
teaching.audioText: Some guests promise to reply later, but the host will not summarise the debate until every claim has been checked.

prompt.es: Elige el informe que respeta la actitud del ingeniero en esta entrevista.

choices.text: The engineer admitted that there had been a fault.
The engineer claimed that there had been a fault.
The engineer denied that there had been a fault.

feedback.es: Reconoce un fallo que le incomoda («we did not notice it»): admit transmite esa actitud, claim la pondría en duda.

hint.es: Piensa si el ingeniero defiende algo discutible o reconoce algo incómodo.

origin.text: Interviewer: Was the bridge closed because of a fault? Engineer: Yes, there was a fault, and we did not notice it soon enough.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los médicos sugieren acostarse antes y advierten contra el café tardío.»

feedback.es: Suggest admite el patrón -ing (suggest going); no podría seguir con to + verbo.

hint.es: El verbo va seguido de going: busca el que admite -ing y significa «proponer».

origin.text: Doctors ___ going to bed earlier, and they warn people against drinking coffee late in the evening.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El gerente admitió haber cometido un grave error el año pasado.»

answer.text: The manager admitted making a serious mistake last year

feedback.es: Admit se construye con -ing cuando el sujeto habla de algo que él mismo hizo.

hint.es: Después del verbo de habla va el gerundio: making.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los investigadores, sin embargo, sostienen que hacen falta más pruebas.»

feedback.es: Maintain that refleja que los investigadores sostienen su postura frente a lo que afirma el folleto.

origin.text: The company's leaflet claims that the drink is safe. Other researchers, however, ___ that more tests are needed before anyone can say so.

prompt.es: ¿Qué informe recoge fielmente lo que dijo el entrenador tras el partido?

choices.text: The coach denied that the team had played badly and promised to change it.
The coach admitted that the team had played badly and refused to change it.
The coach claimed that the team had played badly and suggested changing it.

feedback.es: Reconoce que jugaron mal y se niega a cambiar el equipo: los otros informes invierten o deforman una de las dos ideas.

origin.text: Coach: «I will be honest with you: we played badly. I will not make excuses, and I will not change the team on Saturday.»

prompt.es: Cuenta con un verbo de habla lo que dijo el médico.

answer.text: The doctor warned us not to drink coffee after six o'clock.
accepted: The doctor warned us not to drink coffee after six o'clock.
The doctor warned us not to drink coffee after six.
The doctor warned people not to drink coffee after six o'clock.

feedback.es: Warn + persona + not to + verbo transmite una advertencia; el médico no se limita a decir algo: avisa de un riesgo.

origin.text: Doctor: «Do not drink coffee after six o'clock: it is bad for your sleep.»

prompt.es: Escucha el debate y elige el resumen más fiel de la postura de la directora.

choices.text: She denies that the timetable causes problems and promises to cancel it.
She claims the change is perfect and suggests using it in every school.
She admits there are problems but refuses to cancel the change for now.

feedback.es: Reconoce que el horario no es perfecto, pero se niega a cancelarlo antes de tener resultados de un año completo.

origin.audio: At the end of the radio debate, the head of the school defends the new timetable. It is not perfect, she admits, and lessons now start earlier than many families would like. Even so, she maintains that students concentrate better in the morning, and she refuses to cancel the change before a full year of results is available. Asked about the cost of the extra buses, she promises to publish every figure next month, but she downplays the complaints from parents.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué da a entender al negarse a cancelar el cambio ahora.

choices.text: That she wants clear results before deciding on the change.
That she expects the parents to stop complaining soon.
That she doubts the change will bring any benefit at all.

feedback.es: Condiciona la decisión a un año completo de resultados: pide pruebas antes de juzgar, no anticipa ni el fracaso ni el éxito.

origin.audio: At the end of the radio debate, the head of the school defends the new timetable. It is not perfect, she admits, and lessons now start earlier than many families would like. Even so, she maintains that students concentrate better in the morning, and she refuses to cancel the change before a full year of results is available. Asked about the cost of the extra buses, she promises to publish every figure next month, but she downplays the complaints from parents.

prompt.es: Completa: «El gerente se negó a comentar hasta que se publicaran los resultados.»

feedback.es: Refuse to + verbo expresa una negativa directa; promise to + verbo, en cambio, compromete a hacer algo después.

origin.text: Asked about the missing money, the manager ___ to comment until the results were published, although he promised to reply later.

prompt.es: Cuenta con tres verbos de habla lo que dice una compañera en su nota.

answer.text: My colleague admits making a mistake in the third table, warns that the figures may be wrong, and promises to send a corrected version on Monday.
accepted: My colleague admits making a mistake in the third table, warns that the figures may be wrong, and promises to send a corrected version on Monday.
My colleague admitted making a mistake in the third table, warned us that the figures might be wrong and promised to send a corrected version on Monday.
My colleague acknowledges that he made a mistake in the third table, warns that the figures may be wrong, and promises to send a corrected version on Monday.

feedback.es: El resumen fiel convierte cada idea en un verbo de habla con su patrón: admit + -ing, warn + that, promise + to.

origin.text: Note from a colleague: «I made a mistake in the third table. The figures may be wrong. Please do not share the report before Friday, and I will send a corrected version on Monday.»

prompt.es: Lee el comunicado del ayuntamiento. ¿Qué resumen es fiel?

choices.text: The council promises that the bridge will reopen in June without any further problems.
The council regrets the delay and acknowledges that the June date is not guaranteed.
The council denies that there has been a delay and urges residents to wait.

feedback.es: El comunicado lamenta el retraso y deja la fecha de junio abierta a nuevos problemas: no promete ni niega nada.

origin.text: Council statement: «We regret the delay. The bridge will reopen in June, although we cannot rule out further problems. Residents who use the old route should plan for extra time.»

prompt.es: Ordena: «Varios expertos señalan que la muestra era demasiado pequeña.»

answer.text: Several experts point out that the sample was far too small

feedback.es: Point out + that introduce el dato que el hablante señala; la oración subordinada mantiene el orden sujeto + verbo.

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud transmite la directora en esta respuesta a un periodista?

choices.text: She downplays the problem by blaming the supplier alone.
She flatly denies that anyone in the company knew.
She concedes that the company was slow but shares the blame.

feedback.es: Acepta su parte del error («we should have acted sooner»), pero añade que el proveedor tampoco ayudó: reconoce sin cargar toda la culpa.

origin.text: Journalist: Did the company know about the fault? Director: We found out about it in March, and I accept that we should have acted sooner, although the supplier did not help either.
